attributes.body_ja:
「それなら」は、前（まえ）の発言（はつげん）が事実（じじつ）であれば、(B) も恐（おそ）らく成立（せいりつ）する、または (B) を考（かんが）えるべきだ、と言（い）いたいときに使（つか）われる接続詞（せつぞくし）です。「もしそうなら (B)」や「その場合（ばあい）は (B)」のような意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。

「それなら」は、相手（あいて）の発言（はつげん）に対（たい）して返事（へんじ）をするときに最（もっと）もよく使（つか）われます。話（はな）し手（て）が相手（あいて）の発言（はつげん）を受（う）けて、予想（よそう）や提案（ていあん）、または意見（いけん）を述（の）べるときの表現（ひょうげん）です。

「だったら」や「それだったら」という言（い）い方（かた）も「それなら」と同（おな）じ意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。
attributes.body:
Acting as a conjunction, それなら is a structure used for highlighting that if the previous statement is the case, then (B) will probably also be true, or will need to be considered. それなら may be interpreted as 'if that's the case, then (B)'.

それなら is most often used when replying to some statement that the speaker has just heard from another person. In these cases, it will come before some sort of guess, suggestion, or consideration about what the speaker has just heard.

だったら and それだったら may also be seen, and carry the same meaning.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.description: その場合は VS それなら

attributes.body: それなら and それでは can both be used at the start of a sentence as transition markers meaning in that case or well then. それなら expresses a response to a specific condition, as in それなら行きません (In that case, I won’t go). それでは can overlap in usage, but it can also mean well then or and with that, often used to wrap up a topic, as in それでは、失礼します (Well then, excuse me), which それなら cannot convey.3

second_relatable.title: では・それでは・じゃあ
second_relatable.meaning: If so, Well (then), In that case

attributes.body: なら follows a phrase or noun to express a condition, as in 田中さんが行かないなら、私も行かない (If Tanaka isn’t going, I won’t go either). The なら of それなら is the same particle, but the phrase それなら is used sentence-initially to refer back to something previously mentioned, as in 行かないの？それなら私も行かない (You’re not going? In that case, I won’t go either).

second_relatable.title: なら
second_relatable.meaning: Were it, If, If it's the case, As for (Conditional)

attributes.body: それなら expresses a response to a condition, as in それなら行きません (In that case, I won’t go). The conditional たら form can also mark conditions at the end of verbs, adjectives, or nouns. それだったら can convey a similar meaning to それなら, but with a slight nuance: それなら assumes the condition will or has happened, while それだったら tends to be more hypothetical.3

second_relatable.title: たら
second_relatable.meaning: When, From when, Just when, If
